correctness.rationale: An unordered uniformly sampled source triple has one, two, or three distinct successors. If all equal, strict peak impossible; two-image case forces the unique-image source centrally and yields the only linear position term from one-target-inside/one-outside motifs. For three distinct images, non-invariant triples give 1/3 by uniform ordering, whereas invariant triple permutations produce precisely all-fixed and cyclic-three corrections. Sum over C(n,3) triples gives slope and centered intercept. Checked n=4 exhaustively for all 256 maps and all 24 relabelings against formula at both interior indices with exact rationals; proof handles arbitrary n and possible ties, not inferred from the check.

originality.rationale: Existing peak generating functions for uniform permutations and fixed permutation conjugacy classes cover the bijective specialization and should not be claimed new. Those formulations assume distinct outputs, while arbitrary many-to-one mappings have genuine ties; the two signed coalescence motifs M_+,M_- and their positional slope provide a new exact noninjective law. A known cycle/peak covariance for random permutations has a different random variable. No published exact mapping-conjugacy profile implying this signed coalescence formula was identified.

value.rationale: Local peaks of relabeled functional digraphs connect mapping structure (indegrees, fixed points, cycles and coalescence motifs) with order-statistic patterns. A universal affine profile and combinatorial slope-sign rule for every finite endofunction is a meaningful structural law beyond permutation-only cases.

final_claim: For any deterministic f:[n]->[n] with n>=4, uniform conjugation by a permutation gives exact interior strict-peak probabilities p_i that are affine in i, with slope (M_+-M_-)/(3*C(n,3)*(n-3)) and mean depending only on indegree triple collisions, fixed points, and 3-cycles.
limitations: One-site strict peaks only, no joint peak law or function reconstruction; n>=4.
